summary: Iteration 6 (chunked upload + auth refresh + dashboard plan reflection): All 4 fixes VERIFIED end-to-end. Added 13 new backend tests (TestAuthRefreshIter6=6 + TestChunkedUploadIter6=5 + TestDashboardStatsPlanReflection=2) - ALL 13 PASS. Full backend suite 62/70 pass; the 8 failures are pre-existing Razorpay LIVE-key/Cloudflare throttling (documented since iteration 4 - _create_order_with_retry helper couldn't recover this run because provider was returning HTML 502 pages from Cloudflare instead of clean 502s, so retry loop exited early). Frontend UI: Admin (monthly plan) dashboard shows Plan Validity='355 days' and NO amber warning; fresh no-plan user dashboard shows amber 'No Active Plan' warning and Plan Validity='No Plan' - dashboard fix works perfectly (screenshots saved). Chunked upload UI: uploaded /tmp/v.mp4 (10,998 bytes) via VideoManager -> upload-progress-container appeared with upload-progress-percent 0->completion, success toast '✅ Ready for the stream! Plan validity: 354 days remaining' rendered top-right, video appeared in grid, and GET /api/videos confirmed persistence with correct size. Rename + Delete regression PASS. Auth refresh backend verified: (a) no cookie -> 401 'No refresh token', (b) valid refresh_token -> 200 + new access_token Set-Cookie, (c) simulated 'expired access, valid refresh' scenario -> refresh issues new token and /auth/me succeeds, (d) invalid JWT rejected 401, (e) sending access_token as refresh rejected 401 'Invalid token type', (f) access token TTL decoded from JWT = ~43200s (12h) confirming the lifetime change.

action_items: (env / not a bug) Razorpay LIVE keys are heavily rate-limited in this preview cluster. For CI reliability either (a) switch to Razorpay TEST keys, or (b) add a retry-after Cloudflare 502 path in _create_order_with_retry, or (c) mark those 3-5 order-creation tests xfail in CI. Server-side create_order is already correct; this is purely a provider/edge throttle.

(deploy) The 413 root-cause in production is nginx client_max_body_size. Iteration-6 chunking (5MB slices) sidesteps it, but confirm deploy/nginx.conf has a matching or larger client_max_body_size for direct API access.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py /api/videos/upload/chunk (lines 471-545): correctly namespaces the tmp part file by user_id (prevents cross-user collisions/abuse), incrementally enforces the 2GB budget against part_path.stat().st_size (verified by test), and wipes stale .part on chunk_index==0 (verified by test test_chunk_upload_first_chunk_wipes_previous_partial). Edge cases NOT covered: (a) if a client aborts mid-upload the .part file is never cleaned up server-side; recommend a periodic janitor over uploads/tmp/. (b) no total_chunks==0 guard - if a bad client sends total_chunks=0 the endpoint would still create a zero-byte video on chunk_index==0 (since chunk_index+1 < total_chunks fails); low severity but consider validating total_chunks >= 1.

server.py /api/auth/refresh (lines 317-341): reads refresh_token cookie, verifies type=='refresh', issues new access_token with 12h TTL. Correct. Nice-to-have: rotate refresh_token on refresh (currently only access_token is rotated) so that a leaked refresh_token has finite lifetime; today refresh_token remains valid for its full 7d regardless of how many times it's used.

api.js interceptor (lines 15-48): single-flight guard via refreshPromise is present but there is a subtle race - if request A hits 401 first and starts a refresh, and request B hits 401 before A's interceptor sets isRefreshing=true (they're on different microtasks), B could start a second refresh. In practice fine since /auth/refresh is idempotent, but consider setting isRefreshing before creating the promise.

api.js chunked upload (lines 107-153): sequential (not parallel) - correct choice for order-preservation but SLOW for large files. The per-chunk retry only retries once and doesn't distinguish network vs 4xx errors, so a 403 (plan expired mid-upload) would be retried unnecessarily. Minor.

server.py access token TTL is now 12h (line 124). This is a security-vs-UX tradeoff - the previous 15m was more secure. Consider shortening it back once the auto-refresh interceptor is proven stable in prod, or making it configurable via env.
server.py is 1382 lines - still recommend splitting into APIRouter modules (flagged since iteration 2).

rca of the issue: USER REPORT: 4 critical bugs - (1) 413 Request Entity Too Large on video upload, (2) 'Not Authenticated' during upload, (3) upload stops on tab-switch, (4) active plan not reflecting on Dashboard. RCA: (1) whole-file multipart POST hit nginx client_max_body_size; (2) 15-minute access token expired mid-upload of large files; (3) related to (2) - tab throttling caused the single long-lived request to be paused past the 15m mark; (4) Dashboard read plan from stale AuthContext user object (never refreshed after purchase). FIXES verified: (1) chunked upload sends 5MB slices sequentially to /api/videos/upload/chunk - no single request exceeds proxy limits; (2) access_token lifetime bumped to 12h AND axios interceptor auto-refreshes via /api/auth/refresh on 401 and retries the original request; (3) same as (2) - each 5MB chunk is a short request that completes before any tab-throttling could kill it, and each chunk is independently retried once; (4) Dashboard now sources planId/planExpiry from /api/dashboard/stats first (falls back to user context) and calls refreshUser() on mount. All four fixes independently verified by pytest tests and browser automation.
